chunks: And from his words (peace be upon him) to one of his companions when he decided to set out for the Kharijites, he said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, if you set out at this time, I fear according to the science of astrology that you will not achieve your aim,' whereupon he (peace be upon him) said:

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali.
key_terms.الْخَوَارِجِ: The Kharijites, a early Islamic sect known for their rebellion against Ali.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the predictions of astrologers regarding his campaign against the Kharijites?
ai.summary: In this episode from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) responds to a companion’s anxiety about military timing based on 'ilm al-nujum' (astrology), asserting that divine decree supersedes celestial influences. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that while stars may have natural effects, they do not dictate fate, which remains under Allah’s sole control. The incident underscores the practical application of tawhid in leadership, where trust in God outweighs reliance on omens or astronomical calculations.
